Leave Your Second Phone at Home: Multi-Account Trading Is Here

Trade multiple accounts at the same time: assign a leader and pick which accounts follow it. More accounts filled, fewer moves missed, and the same two rules as always.

November 15, 2026 · 3 min read
On this page

  • Try it out

Leader accounts, follower accounts, matching every order between them, and the right sizing options that fit your risk.

We listen to what traders have to say. Switching tabs, screens, or even devices to take the same trade with the same firm is crazy. We had to do something about that, so you get all your accounts filled before the bounce.

Here is every detail on what it is, how it works, and what stays the same:

What is multi-account trading?

Instead of placing the same trade on every single account, you can now set up a leader account and choose which accounts should follow.

  • One account leads, the rest follow.
    • You choose which account is which and mix evals with funded accounts in whatever way you want.
  • You only interact with your leader account.
    • Set it up once, and you never have to touch your followers again. Trade on your leader and your followers match every move you make.

Try it out

  1. Open the web terminal or the Breakout app.
  2. Check if you have at least two active Breakout accounts. Need another? Pay with Payouts, no need to leave the portal.
  3. For web: open the menu in the top-right corner. For the app: open the portfolio tab.
  4. Select Multi-account trading, choose your leader, choose your followers, and pick a sizing option.

Size matters

There are two sizing options.

  • Exact: every follower matches the position size of the leader.
    • A $1,000 loss on your $100,000 leader account = a $1,000 loss on your $50,000 follower account.
    • The $100,000 account took a 1% loss, but for the $50,000 account that exact $1,000 is a 2% loss.
  • Proportional: every follower matches the relative risk of the leader.
    • A $1,000 loss on your $100,000 leader account = a $500 loss on your $50,000 follower account.
    • Both accounts took the same proportional loss: 1%.

Check your settings before you max long all your accounts into max drawdown.

How do followers follow?

Follower accounts follow everything, not just your entries.

  • Entry, SL or TP.
  • Move or cancel any of them on your leader and the followers follow.
  • Closing your position? The followers close too.

If your leader account gets breached, all following stops.

When a follower can’t follow

Every account has its own rules. They do not change when following. If one of your accounts can’t take the same trade as its leader, it gets skipped. You can read the reason for every skip in your trade history. Every other follower still follows, so one buzzkill doesn’t ruin the party.

Get Breakout updates in your inbox

Platform releases, trader interviews, and product updates from the Breakout team. No spam, unsubscribe anytime.

What did not change

Every account still has the same simple set of rules: max daily loss and max drawdown. The limit on your combined account size, eval and funded, is still $200,000. So you can run up to 40 $5,000 accounts at the same time, if that’s your thing.

This. Is. Not. Copy. Trading.

You can’t use it to copy that bottom ticker on your timeline. Multi-account trading only works on your own accounts.

Every follower follows the direction of the leader, so it is not a hedging tool either. Hedging between accounts is how you get breached. It is strictly against our terms of service. Hedging within the same account is perfectly fine, so if your leader is hedged, your followers will be too.

Multi-account trading is available in the Breakout Terminal on web and mobile.

Follow the leader

If you have not traded with us for a while because your risk manager put you on a strict one-phone-per-firm limit, now is the time to come back and check us out. If you are still running accounts with us, we appreciate your support more than you know.

We are on a legendary run: $80M+ paid to traders, on demand.
wen $100M?

Your old phone can finally retire: you only need one to get all your accounts filled now.
